acme_jane: Hey support, after upgrading our client lib to 2.3.1 our embeddings calls suddenly return vectors of length 384 but our app expects 1536. No code changes other than the pip upgrade. Repro below, any clue?

acme_jane: curl we use (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \\n  -H \"Authorization: Bearer xxxxx\" \\n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8\" \\n  -d '\\{"input": "[[0.012, 0.34, 0.21, ... , 0.003]]", "model":"embed-large-1536"}'
```

acme_jane: Response is 200 but embedding length is 384. Error only started after client lib update.

mike_support: Thanks — can you paste the full request body exactly as the server sees it (headers + body) and confirm whether you're sending a batch or a single input? Also, which SDK or requests code are you calling?

acme_jane: We send one item per call (batch size 1). Our Python wrapper does something like: `payload = json.dumps({"input": json.dumps(vec)})` then `requests.post(..., data=payload, headers=headers)`.

acme_jane: We also tried with the new official client which constructs `client.embeddings.create(input=json.dumps(vec))` and saw the same result.

mike_support: That double `json.dumps` is suspicious. It means the server is receiving the `input` field as a JSON string (i.e. the literal characters `"[0.012, ...]"`) instead of a numeric array. When an array of numbers is stringified, the embeddings endpoint treats it as text rather than a numeric vector payload and the model routing/fallback can change (and return a different-dimension embedding).

alex_eng: Confirming from runtime logs for your org id: incoming body had `"input": "[0.012,0.34,...]"` (string). The service attempted the text-embedding path, which for the selected model family maps to a 384-dim comparator vector in our current catalog. We also saw a model-routing fallback because the numeric-array shape wasn't detected.

mike_support: Quick repro you can run locally to see the difference:
```bash
# broken (stringified inner array)
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input": "[0.1,0.2,0.3]", "model":"embed-large-1536"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings | jq

# fixed (real array)
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input": [0.1,0.2,0.3], "model":"embed-large-1536"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings | jq
```
You should see different vector lengths between the two.

mike_support: Also, avoid `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8` being combined with manual `data=` + `json.dumps` in some clients — using `requests.post(json=payload)` or the SDK's `client.embeddings.create(input=...)` with a proper Python list will ensure correct encoding.

acme_jane: Ah, we discovered our wrapper was calling `json.dumps` twice when payloads came from an older helper. We changed to `payload = {"input": vec}` and `requests.post(..., json=payload)` and retested.

acme_jane: Fixed — embeddings are now 1536 long again. Thanks! :party_parrot:

alex_eng: Nice. To summarize for the ticket: root cause was client-side double-encoding of the numeric vector (sent as JSON string) which routed the call down the text-embedding path (different model variant/dimension). We've added a small snippet to the support KB and an example in the SDK docs to show correct vs incorrect encodings.

mike_support: I'll mark this resolved but leaving a short repro attached to the case for posterity. If you want, we can run a quick audit on other endpoints to ensure no similar double-encode code paths exist in your wrapper.

acme_jane: Please do the audit — we had a few utilities that stringify payloads by default. Happy to share the small helper we fixed.

sre_bot: Incident note: no infra issue found; classified as client-encoding/user-error. Logged as support-3123456789 in the tracker.

mike_support: Closing here. If anything else pops up ping me directly. :thumbsup:
